subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the requested fix changes sandbox write-boundary semantics that current tests and docs still encode as read-restricted.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require one coherent implementation across Docker/browser mounts, fs bridges, tool exposure, docs, and regression proof.

options.title: Keep `none` read-only
options.body: Preserve the current security default, document that `none` is intentionally read-restricted, and route users to `rw` or future explicit writable-isolated configuration.

options.title: Fold into bind design
options.body: Defer the exact semantic change and resolve it together with the broader least-privilege writable bind work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require one coherent implementation across Docker/browser mounts, fs bridges, tool exposure, docs, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original behavior and follow-up tests, making him the best available owner for the sandbox security-boundary decision.
